articleTitle: Knowledge based systems lifecycle models within the KADS methodology
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Expert Systems Lifecycle
abstract: Summary form only given as follows. The paper indicates the current thinking within ESPRIT project 1098-KADS in terms of lifecycle models for knowledge based systems development. It discusses various approaches to this problem and commits itself firmly to a hierarchical spiral model description of the development process.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Structured prototyping for requirements specification of expert systems
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Expert Systems Lifecycle
abstract: The author describes three kinds of prototyping, evolutionary, revolutionary and revelationary. Evolutionary prototyping is used when the target system may be constructed in the original prototyping language, with suitable third generation language extensions. He concentrates on the benefits of this approach and the changes to the conventional system life-cycle which have to be made.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Lessons learned from industrial expert systems
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Expert Systems Lifecycle
abstract: The relative newness of the field means that industrial experience with expert systems relate mostly to the earlier stages of the system life-cycle. For convenience these are listed under two categories. The first is Orientation, which covers the way in which the project is set up initially. The second category covers Development of the expert system. The points given cover some of the more obvious results of experience under these two categories, presented in the form of hints to developers of future industrial expert systems.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Expert Systems Lifecycle
abstract: The most advanced projects in British Steel are in the process control domain with large systems in advanced stages of development. As an example of the approach taken the intelligent Kiln Controller project is described.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Expert systems for life, not just for Christmas: a financial application
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Expert Systems Lifecycle
abstract: Describes work carried out by the UK Knowledge Engineering Group of Coopers and Lybrand, in providing expert system support for the substantive test program used when planning an audit. An expert system called Expertest was developed. Its aims were to reduce the skill level required to complete a substantive test programme and to speed the completion of the substantive test programme when performed by experienced staff. The author also looks at their Knowledge Based Maintenance System.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Learning about a control domain through expert systems
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Expert Systems Lifecycle
abstract: The basis theme of the paper is that tasks which entail dealing with significant amounts of complexity and uncertainty require for their solution a symbiotic partnership of man and machine. In teaching control engineering, this viewpoint leads to a concern with developing knowledge based support systems (KBSS) rather than autonomous expert systems. These systems must be integrated with a human, so that they are flexible enough not to constrain the human's powerful reasoning methods and at the same time are capable of teaching control engineers about new design methods. MAID is a prototype system, which has been implemented in the domain of multivariable frequency domain control systems design. An important function of MAID is to teach control engineers new design methods. The designer learns how to generate controllers that manipulate the systems frequency characteristics into a form satisfying the design objectives. The ideas outlined have been used to develop a KBSS for the Multivariable Control toolbook built on top of the MATLAB environment.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>
